claim.claim-text: 2. The method of claim 1, wherein the parameters of the trained variant pathogenicity prediction model have been further tuned based on missense training example sequence pairs and supplemental training position frequency matrices.

3. The method of claim 2, wherein a supplemental training position frequency matrix of the supplemental training position frequency matrices is identical to a position frequency matrix of a missense training example sequence pair at a start location and an end location.

4. The method of claim 3, wherein the parameters of the trained variant pathogenicity prediction model have been further tuned to attenuate a training influence of the supplemental training position frequency matrices.

5. The method of claim 2, wherein a supplemental training position frequency matrix of the supplemental training position frequency matrices includes amino-acid locations from data for non-human primates or non-primate mammals.
6. The method of claim 1, wherein each supplemental training example amino-acid sequence pair comprises a reference amino-acid sequence and an alternative amino-acid sequence.

7. The method of claim 6, wherein each supplemental training example amino-acid sequence pair comprises a supplemental benign training example amino-acid sequence pair including a start location, through a target amino acid location, to an end location.

8. The method of claim 7, wherein the start location and the end location of each supplemental training example amino-acid sequence pair respectively match a start location and an end location of a corresponding missense variant training example amino-acid sequence pair.

9. The method of claim 6, wherein each supplemental training example amino-acid sequence pair comprises a supplemental benign training example amino-acid sequence pair that matches a start location and an end location of a corresponding missense variant training example amino acid sequence pair that includes a variant.

10. The method of claim 1, wherein the ensemble of networks of the trained variant pathogenicity prediction model have been tuned together as part of ensemble training based on supplemental benign training example sequence pairs.
11. The method of claim 1, wherein providing at least the position frequency matrix to the trained variant pathogenicity prediction model comprises providing one or more of:

12. The method of claim 1, wherein generating the pathogenicity prediction for the variant amino acid comprises determining a mean of the pathogenicity predictions determined by the ensemble of networks.
13. The method of claim 1, wherein the ensemble of networks of the trained variant pathogenicity prediction model comprise an ensemble of neural networks.

14. A system including one or more processors coupled to memory, the memory loaded with computer instructions, when executed on the one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to perform a method according to any one of claims 1-13.

15. A non-transitory computer readable storage medium impressed with computer program instructions, when executed on one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to perform a method according to any one of claims 1-13.
